title: Going to New Orleans with Tom Albert's band
summary: He joined Tom Albert's band, toured Texas, and recalls knowing few New Orleans musicians beforehand.

trombones. Excuse me sir. Clowns on banjo, they call them dad. Oh, they're clowns friends? Yeah, dad, um, banjo and myself. You were playing clowns still? Yeah. What was that at? Oh, we played, oh, a lot of different places. We were in Texas, stayed out there three weeks from Texas.
What was the name of the band? Tom Albert and Bones. Did they ever call him Kid Albert? Yeah, that's right. Kid Albert and Bones.
Did you know any of the musicians personally from New Orleans before you went there? You know, I mean, they're really friendly with them. What did you sort of?

No, I never say I'm by seeing him. I know Joe Watson because every time he'd come, he'd have to be around Joe. And I knew Alfred Williams. He was coming here with me. And I know Tom because Tom used to stay back there with that miles when he'd get off at night when he'd get to the train or in the morning go back to New Orleans. And I didn't know too many, too many fellas. Did you get to know him quickly? Oh, after I got in New Orleans, yeah, I was getting to know him a lot because everyone around there wanted me to play with him. Yeah. And I wouldn't need Tom for none of them because of the fact that he was the one who brought me there and he was the same as a father to me. I stayed in his house and ate and slept and he didn't cost me a nickel. And I stayed with him about five, six years. What, the Fledgings band all the time? Yeah. You could hire me if you didn't have nothing. For that night I'd go play with you, but if you had something, you could hire me. What other bands did you play around with?
